title: Biologic Characterization of Patients With ITP
off: Biologic Characterization of Patients With Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP)
summary: This is a no-profit, multicenter, biological, non-pharmacologic study aimed to characterize from a biological point of view previously untreated primary ITP patients. To this end, peripheral blood, fecal and bone marrow samples will be collected at baseline and at 30 days and 180 days after treatment initiation - for each line of therapy - and the results of the biological analysis performed at each time point will then be compared.
desc:
This is a no-profit, multicenter, biological, non-pharmacologic study aimed to characterize from a biological point of view ITP patients. Patients with previously untreated primary ITP who need first-line therapy will be included in the study.

To this end, peripheral blood, fecal and bone marrow samples will be collected at baseline and at 30 days and 180 days after treatment initiation. The same assessments will be repeated in case of any potential new line of therapy.

The results of the biological analysis performed at each time point will then be compared, in order to seek changes related to the natural history of the disease, the therapy administered and the response achieved.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Patients with primary ITP, in need for first line treatment according to 2019 ITP consensus2.
2. Previously untreated patients. Patients who have already started first-line therapy because of life-threatening bleeding are admitted to the study if samples are collected within 24 hours of starting treatment. In such cases, as first-line treatment steroids and platelet transfusions would be preferable over high-dose IVIg. Treatment received before the collection of samples will be carefully documented.
3. Age ≥ 18 years
4. Signed written informed consent according to ICH/EU/GCP and national local laws.

Exclusion Criteria:

1\. Secondary ITP. Patients with ANA positivity without a diagnosis of SLE are admitted to the study. As far as patients with ITP and antiphospholipid antibodies positivity, those with triple positivity (anti-beta2glicoprotein antibodies, anti-cardiolipin antibodies, lupus anticoagulans positivity) are excluded.

x.titre: Caractérisation biologique des patients atteints de PTI primaire non traité
x.question: Quelles anomalies biologiques caractérisent le PTI primaire avant traitement, et comment évoluent-elles sous traitement ?
x.contexte:
Le purpura thrombopénique immunologique (PTI) primaire est une thrombopénie auto-immune dont les mécanismes sont multiples : auto-anticorps antiplaquettaires, dysrégulation des lymphocytes T, altération de la production plaquettaire. La réponse aux traitements varie fortement d'un patient à l'autre, sans marqueur prédictif utilisable en pratique.

Cette étude non lucrative, multicentrique et non médicamenteuse, promue par le groupe italien GIMEMA, caractérise sur le plan biologique des adultes atteints de PTI primaire qui nécessitent un traitement de première ligne selon le consensus 2019. Des prélèvements de sang périphérique, de selles et de moelle sont réalisés à l'inclusion, puis 30 et 180 jours après le début de chaque ligne de traitement. Les résultats sont comparés pour rechercher des modifications liées à l'histoire naturelle de la maladie, au traitement reçu et à la réponse obtenue.
x.interet: Elle pourrait identifier des signatures biologiques (y compris le microbiote) prédictives de la réponse, pour mieux choisir les traitements dans le PTI.
